selection: Among calibration pairs, SHA256-json sort first-passive agent templates with exposure-unseen verbs; use indices [4:8] from each of 24 target pairs, disjoint from ML-089's [0:4]
question_counterfactual: same entire sentence, agent vs patient single-token cue; all four voice-by-position constructions preserve event semantics

interventions.method: Mask attention FROM the role, event, or who question-token KEY TO ALL strictly later positions, from a specified block through the final transformer block. No activation donor.
interventions.control: first/second event-cue key and fixed who key
interventions.sanity: Cutting the role-key path from layer 1 through all layers must make agent/patient logits identical. This is a structural check, NOT the empirical discovery.

primary_exploratory_question: Among target second-passive questions, is target-pair 2-choice role accuracy substantially higher than native 4-choice accuracy, including on native wrong-event predictions? How does removal of role-key access from L2 onward change role-conditioned target-pair logit evidence relative to event and who control cuts, in each exposure arm?
summary_comparison: Paired target-minus-familiar arm contrast in the role-cut-vs-who-cut effect on role-antisymmetric target-pair logit evidence for second-passive, also report second-active and first-passive controls.
metrics: two-choice target-role accuracy conditional on wrong-event native output
pairwise agent/patient evidence and flip rates
interpretation: No confirmation claim. Even strong two-choice performance need not show native event binding: two-choice decoding supplies the target pair externally. Cutting a token key may produce generic out-of-distribution disruption and paths can be redundant. The main question is information-flow dependence, not a proof of a circuit.
safety: Never invoke protected_target_cases or ML-088 protected cases; never rerun ML-089; one-time ML-090 calibration discovery report.
